title: Joint continuity of the product density derivative
statement: Let $I$ be a finite set and let $v\ge 0$. The product Gaussian density derivative, viewed as a continuous linear functional on $\mathbb R^I$, is jointly continuous as a function of its mean vector $c\in\mathbb R^I$ and input vector $z\in\mathbb R^I$.
replaced: Let $I$ be finite and $v\ge0$. Write $p_v(c,z)$ for the $N(c,v)$ density when $v>0$ and set $p_0(c,z)=0$; define $G_v(c,z)=\prod_{i\in I}p_v(c_i,z_i)$ and interpret division by zero as zero. Let $A_v(c,z)$ be the linear functional $h\mapsto\sum_i\bigl(\prod_{j\ne i}p_v(c_j,z_j)\bigr)((z_i-c_i)/v)p_v(c_i,z_i)h_i$. For each fixed $v\ge0$, $(c,z)\mapsto A_v(c,z)$ is continuous in operator norm.
